title: Auditing Google's Search Algorithm: Measuring News Diversity Across Brazil, the UK, and the US

live_model.evidence: Sec. 3.3.2: "These were incremented with using GPT-4 ... Gpt-4o-2024-05-13 was used to label the remaining sources using the same classification system ... Temperature was set to 0.0. These resulted in an additional 307 ratings."

prompt.location: Sec. 3.3.1/3.3.2 (described only: "the prompt constrained the system to the desired section labels and allowed it to abstain")
prompt.note: Classification instructions are paraphrased, not quoted.

claim.metric: none usable (no accuracy/agreement % reported specifically for the GPT-4o-labeled subset)
claim.location: Sec. 3.3.2 (307 additional political-bias ratings; validation described qualitatively, not as a percentage)

data.source: Authors' own scraped Google Search/Trends results (Sec. 3); MBFC, All Sides and Ad Fontes Media bias ratings used for validation

notes: GPT-4o is used only as a political-bias annotator for 307 sources not covered by Media Bias/Fact Check (role A), with no prompt text quoted and no clean accuracy figure for that subset (validation is described qualitatively: outlets either had 'no political bias' or matched other rating services). An earlier, separate news-section classifier uses gpt-3.5-turbo-1106 (dead preview, outside project scope). The paper's core contribution is a search-audit study, not an LLM capability claim.
